what: Photo cards (up to 18) travel straight around an ellipse in the middle of the board, one lap per 90s. No perspective: the lower (front) a card, the bigger (.76→1x) and darker (.55→1), the upper (back) smaller and fainter, and stacking order puts front on top. Cards are spaced evenly by ‹visible length›, the perimeter divided by each card’s size at that spot. The ellipse and card width (8.5% of board width, 22% on phone) are fitted to avoid the clear area in the middle (the intro text). The ring lags behind the mouse by ±14·±9px (.05 per frame), dragging spins it by the dragged amount, on release it glides to a stop at .08 per second, and scroll speed adds extra rotation. Hovering a card stops it with .6s power2.out, and leaving restarts it with 1.2s power2.inOut (the card lifts 8% and scales 1.06x in .5s). Intro: with burst, cards start stacked in the center, on fx:card the first card rises from below the screen tilted 8° with 1.2s expo.out, on fx:burst the rest scatter into the ring in shuffled order (.012 apart) with 1.6s expo.inOut, and start rotating with 2s sine.inOut. Otherwise they turn on in shuffled order, 40ms apart, over 1.4s

options.width: Card width (share of board width), default .085 — shrinks itself if the perimeter runs short
options.spread: Minimum share to stretch the ellipse to the panel edge, default .7 · spread-narrow default .97
options.tilt-x: Horizontal width the ring shifts with the mouse (px, both sides combined), default 28 · tilt-y default 18
options.hold: If 「none」, it does not pause over the card
options.intro: ‹burst› waits stacked in the center, then scatters on the fx:card and fx:burst events (link it with the loader)
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Board holding the cards — shifts with the mouse
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Rotating card (a link allowed — dragging and releasing blocks the click)
options.[data-fx-part=face]: Photo plate inside the card — lifts on hover
options.[data-fx-part=clear]: Center space to leave empty (intro text) — the ellipse avoids it

note: The original hands off to Web Animations (181 keyframes) once the ring is fully unfolded — here a single ticker line computes the same positions all the way through. The original’s depth overlap was used only on entry and followed document order going back, but here the front item is always on top.
